 Beyond heavy trucks: How Tata eyes growth through Iveco’s engines
 The strategy could open additional revenue streams for the combined enterprise, although established competitors and the cost of developing new customers will test its profitability
 By Amit Vijay Mohile 
 Updated - November 04, 2026 at 09:39 PM. × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/beyond-heavy-trucks-how-tata-eyes-growth-through-ivecos-engines/article71666800.ece Copy Tata Motors is looking beyond heavy trucks to expand Iveco’s industrial engine business, targeting opportunities in agriculture, construction equipment, marine applications and power generation.
 The strategy could open additional revenue streams for the combined enterprise, although established competitors and the cost of developing new customers will test its profitability.
 “We do believe that quite a few of FPT’s capabilities can be scaled up in terms of getting into more industrial applications,” Tata Motors Managing Director and CEO Girish Wagh said at Tuesday’s global media interaction in Turin.
 FPT Industrial, Iveco’s engine and powertrain business, manufactures engines and related systems for commercial vehicles, tractors, construction machinery, boats and generators. It supplies Iveco as well as independent equipment manufacturers.
 The business generated €3.33 billion in revenue in 2025, compared with €3.55 billion in 2024, with external customers accounting for 47 per cent. Engine sales declined 7 per cent to approximately 338,900 units, although adjusted operating profit improved to €224 million from €221 million.
 India offers an established starting point. FPT already provides engineering, testing and aftermarket support from Greater Noida. In September 2024, it announced an agreement to license production of its F28 engine at CNH’s Greater Noida facility for New Holland tractors and CASE construction equipment.
 However, expanding beyond existing customers will bring FPT into competition with Cummins, Kirloskar Oil Engines, Perkins and Ashok Leyland, alongside equipment manufacturers producing their own engines.
 “Industrial customers assess an engine on operating cost, reliability, emissions compliance and service support. The opportunity will depend on matching FPT’s technology to local requirements and supporting customers throughout the product’s working life,” said Randheer Singh, founder and CEO of ForeSee Advisors.
 Beyond engines, Iveco brings established European and Latin American operations, light-commercial-vehicle platforms, buses and customer networks. Tata contributes Indian manufacturing scale, cost-conscious engineering, supplier relationships and emerging-market experience.
 “The opportunity is not to make one organisation more like the other. It is to bring out the best in both,” Wagh said.
 The companies could also share engineering and sourcing capabilities, expand their product portfolios and use established distribution networks to enter additional markets.
 For investors, however, the central question is whether these complementary strengths translate into orders, higher margins and cash generation rather than simply a larger business.
 “The opportunity is to turn a wider product and technology portfolio into customer programmes and better returns. Shareholders need to see additional orders, disciplined development spending and cash generation, said an industry analyst in the know of Iveco’s plans
 “Financing costs, capital expenditure and working-capital requirements will influence how much additional operating profit translates into cash. Acquisition-related debt and any equity dilution could also affect shareholder returns.” He further explained
 Execution remains critical. Although FPT’s engine volumes rose 9 per cent year-on-year in the June 2026 quarter, profitability faced pressure from product mix and quality-related investments.
 The next test will be identifying additional industrial customers, developing locally competitive products and demonstrating that higher volumes can deliver stronger earnings and cash flow, the analyst said.
